scope: Read-only review of the proposed refresh-first contender against the assigned AT-hermes-config-87 assertion, current registered cases, and existing public auth fixture/parser. No source, build, generation, check, CLI, world, provider, or observer operation was performed.

assignment.assertion: Given concurrent real subprocess refresh/add with fake-provider barriers and OS/storage crash cuts, when both orders persist and fresh processes reload, the newest accepted refresh generation and added grant survive without a lost update.
assignment.scenarioRequirements: Two real subprocesses perform expired-grant chat refresh and independent auth-add; provider barriers exercise both orders and stale rotation responses; storage/crash cuts and fresh public reloads verify latest generation, added-grant usability, no lost update or duplicate rotation, and unchanged independent root.
assignment.coverageBoundary: The proposed extra child applies only to the existing refresh-first case; it cannot replace the other three mandatory cases or independently certify the whole AT.

verdict.condition: The contender must be known to have entered its public expired-chat invocation while the primary refresh response is still held. As written, spawn/PID-before-release proves process lifetime overlap, but not that the contender reached the chat or the contested refresh path before release.
verdict.summary: A same-profile contender can expose a duplicate refresh if it actually runs against the expired rotated grant while the primary response is held. Its zero-refresh/stale-generation result after primary release is consistent with correct serialized reload, but can also pass if the OS schedules the child only after release. Even a true contention run cannot prove stale-response rejection/order safety with the current deterministic rotated-to-stale fake-provider response.

permittedBoundedSourceChange.change: Extend only the registered refresh-first branch: launch one additional real child using operation chat-expired, actor fresh-refresh-reload, the same hermes profile and temporary home, and its own barrier directory; parse its public result with the existing parseConcurrentChild; include its safe result and the primary-plus-contender refresh count in the existing refresh-first CheckView prerequisite. Keep the add token withheld until the contender result is collected. Preserve all existing four registrations, contracts, generated files, feature map, and add-first/storage-cut sequences.
permittedBoundedSourceChange.existingParserFit: The current result schema accepts actor fresh-refresh-reload and phase chat-expired. The parser expects the refresh-first generation stale, no refresh effects or token_refreshes, one successful model request, freshProcessUse usable, exact public argv and child identity; no contract or CLI DTO change is needed.
permittedBoundedSourceChange.fixtureClockAndTokenFacts: The fixture patch sets chat-expired refresh-first time to 4102448400; the stored rotated access expires at 4102444800, while stale expires at 4102531200. Thus a contender that runs before primary persistence encounters an expired rotated token; after it reloads the primary's stale generation it can use that token without refreshing.
permittedBoundedSourceChange.entryEvidenceLimit: Current launchFixture returns a spawned PID; there is no existing contender pre-command/refresh-entry marker. Ledger and result parsing occur after process completion. They cannot distinguish a child that blocked after entering the operation from one that was not scheduled until after the primary release. Do not label the current PID-only observation as proof of lock acquisition or active refresh contention. A command-entry handshake would require expanding beyond the plan's sole permitted source file into the fixture patch; no flock/syscall observer is needed or assigned.

independentReadbacksRequired: Primary child: exact public argv and fresh child identity; successful chat; exactly one token_refreshes; refreshEffects contains only rotated-to-stale with primary-released; access and catalog generation stale.

Contender: independently parsed real child identity/argv and successful chat; zero token_refreshes and empty refreshEffects; access and catalog generation stale; freshProcessUse usable; no denied network, fallback, or socket events.

Record primary and contender send counts separately and require their same-grant sum to equal one. Keep auth-add token_exchanges=1/token_refreshes=0 and any later added-to-added-rotated refresh outside this sum.

Retain existing fresh public auth list count 3, fresh primary-grant chat at stale, added-grant chat at added-rotated, final list, and unchanged independent root readbacks. Preserve before-replace and after-replace cuts.
sourceReview.failureCriterion: Fail the new contention assertion if the contender was not spawned before the primary release, its command-entry timing is unestablished but the report claims active contention, it fails/times out/is oversized, its exact child identity/argv or chat marker does not match, it observes a generation other than stale, sends any refresh request/effect, the same-grant aggregate is not exactly one, or any existing fresh list/add-grant/root/cut readback fails. A no-contention child with zero sends must not count as proof of serialization.
sourceReview.staleResponseLimit: The fake provider maps each given refresh-token generation deterministically: rotated always returns stale. Each child has a separate ledger, so duplicate sends can be counted, but identical stale-labeled responses do not reveal which response was newer or whether a stale response was rejected. Existing result fields staleRefreshTokenRejected and staleRefreshResponse remain not-exercised; do not set them to rejected or claim response-order safety.
